content.value_statement: Teams often design APIs with inconsistent resources, errors, and versioning. This skill provides patterns, checklists, and templates for REST, GraphQL, gRPC, OpenAPI, and AsyncAPI work.
actual_capabilities: Explains REST resource naming, status codes, pagination, filtering, versioning, rate limiting, and authentication patterns.
Provides GraphQL schema, connection, mutation, query, and field error guidance.
Shows gRPC proto structure, service methods, message design, and status code mapping.
Includes OpenAPI 3.1 and AsyncAPI 3.0 templates for API documentation.
Offers review checklists and common anti-patterns for launch readiness.
limitations: It provides guidance and templates, not a runnable API generator.
It does not validate live OpenAPI or AsyncAPI documents automatically.
It uses generic examples that must be adapted to each domain.
It does not replace security, privacy, or legal review for production APIs.

use_cases.title: Design a new service contract
use_cases.description: Define resources, methods, errors, pagination, and authentication before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Standardize API governance
use_cases.description: Create shared conventions for REST, GraphQL, gRPC, OpenAPI, and AsyncAPI across teams.

use_cases.title: Review API launch readiness
use_cases.description: Check versioning, documentation, error handling, rate limits, and deprecation plans before release.

prompt_templates.title: Review REST basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the API Design Framework to propose resource names, methods, status codes, and error formats for a simple customer profile API.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an OpenAPI outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the API Design Framework to outline an OpenAPI 3.1 contract for a billing API with authentication, pagination, and validation errors.

prompt_templates.title: Compare API styles
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the API Design Framework to compare REST, GraphQL, and gRPC for an internal search service. Recommend one approach with tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a launch-ready API
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the API Design Framework to review this API proposal for versioning, authorization, idempotency, observability, and breaking-change risk: [paste proposal].

output_examples.input: Request: Design a users API for account management.
output_examples.output: A resource model with user endpoints, HTTP methods, status codes, pagination rules, and structured validation error guidance.

output_examples.input: Request: Decide between REST and GraphQL for a dashboard.
output: A comparison of query flexibility, caching, client complexity, and governance.
A recommendation based on consumer needs and operational constraints.

output_examples.input: Request: Prepare event documentation for order processing.
output_examples.output: An AsyncAPI-oriented event map with channels, message names, payload concepts, security schemes, and retry expectations.

best_practices: Start with resource boundaries, consumer workflows, and error semantics before choosing syntax.
Use versioning, deprecation periods, and additive changes to protect existing clients.
Review templates with backend, frontend, security, and platform owners before launch.
anti_patterns: Do not copy example domains, IDs, or payloads into production without adapting them.
Do not expose database tables, internal method names, or implementation details in URLs.
Do not treat template security schemes as final production controls.

faq.question: Does this skill generate working backend code?
faq.answer: No. It guides API design and documentation. You still implement and test the service in your stack.

faq.question: Can it help with OpenAPI and AsyncAPI?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes OpenAPI 3.1 and AsyncAPI 3.0 templates for structured documentation.

faq.question: Does it support GraphQL and gRPC?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers schema design, query patterns, mutation errors, proto structure, and gRPC status code mapping.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production API review?
faq.answer: It supports production review, but teams still need security, privacy, performance, and domain-specific approval.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it call external services?
faq.answer: No. The files are documentation and templates. Example URLs are placeholders, not network requests.
